To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the hierarchy of nested spaces is not the essential core element for multi-resolution modeling; (2) the intermediate meshes resulting from mesh decimation provide the necessary multi-resolution information; (3) the local frame coding of the detail coefficients is the key to an efficient multi-resolution modeling on arbitrary meshes; and (4) multi-resolution modeling on unstructured meshes is a powerful tool for the interactive modification of meshes with complex topology.

(a) the hierarchy of nested spaces can be replaced by a hierarchy of intermediate meshes emerging form incremental mesh decimation; and (b) the combination of mesh hierarchies and local frame coding provides a flexible and intuitive framework for interactive detail-preserving mesh modification.

multi-resolution modeling on arbitrary meshes can be achieved by using incremental mesh decimation and that the resulting multi-resolution representation allows for efficient and intuitive mesh manipulation.
